title: Deferred span queue and async client instrumentation adapter
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description: Implement an SDK middleware and runtime adapter that enables async clients (long‑lived websockets, worker queues, mobile SDKs) to emit tracing spans without increasing request latency or overwhelming the tracing backend. The feature introduces a deferred-span queue with bounded memory, batch flush policies, and lossy propagation for best‑effort contexts when connectivity is intermittent. It also provides a small surface for SDKs to attach lightweight provenance markers so spans can be stitched across hops even when parent contexts are dropped.
design_decisions: Use an in-memory ring buffer per-process with configurable max_entries to avoid unbounded memory growth
Batch flush on size (default 50) or time (default 200ms) to balance latency vs throughput
Provide two propagation modes: strong (full trace context) and best-effort (trace_id only + local sampling) for lossy transports
Expose an opt-in SDK API for attaching a short-lived provenance token (16 bytes) instead of full baggage to reduce header size
Defer synchronous span export for non-critical requests, but keep critical path spans export inline when annotated by caller
implementation_todo: Core: implement ring buffer and batcher with backpressure metrics
SDK: add middleware for Python/Node/Go that integrates with async clients and workers
Propagation: add provenance-token encoder/decoder and header name (X-RDW-Provenance)
Backend: update exporter to accept batched deferred spans with optional provenance header
Testing: fault-injection tests for dropped propagation, memory pressure, and high QPS
Docs: Confluence design doc and SDK changelog entries
Rollout: feature flag + canary on telemetry-2.3 to 10% of hosts, monitor error/latency dashboards
acceptance_criteria: SDKs can enqueue spans without blocking request path under 99th percentile latency SLAs
Deferred-span exporter flushes batches according to configured policies and does not exceed memory budget
Provenance token allows >70% successful stitching of traces for lossy transports in synthetic tests
No increase in P95 request latency for instrumented endpoints after canary (within noise budget)
Production dashboards show exporter error rate <0.1% and acceptable throughput improvements vs immediate-export baseline
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Deferred queue growth during prolonged network outage. Mitigation: eviction policy (drop oldest) and telemetry alert when eviction rate > threshold
Risk: Token collisions or privacy leakage. Mitigation: token derived from HMAC of request id with rotation and no user data included
Risk: Increased tracing backend load during flush storms. Mitigation: jittered flush and exponential backoff on exporter failures
Risk: SDK adoption friction. Mitigation: provide drop-in middleware with sane defaults and automated migration guide
